chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Arrangers in the Tommy Miles band
summary: Most of Miles's book was written, by arrangers like Jimmy Mundy, Elton Hill and Garnett Clark.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Which is the way the bands that you were with did, right?

Well, most of the ones I was with, except for Booker Coleman and the Hot Chocolates, they were written arrangements. Tommy Miles and all -- almost everything Tommy Miles had was -- they were written arrangements. Naturally you made up a few things, you know, but most of the things were written because he had -- he had an abundance of good arrangers over there, you know, Tommy Miles did. He couldn't write himself but he had several arrangers in that band.

Elton Hill, Warren Jefferson, Warner Carter, trumpet player. He had about five or six. A piano player used to be with the band, he wrote -- Garnett Clark, the young guy I mentioned. And he had about six or seven real pretty good
